arxiv-2111-05812.title: A study of sunspot 3 minute oscillations using ALMA and GST Journal: ApJ
arxiv-2111-05812.creator: Yi Chai, Dale E. Gary, Kevin P. Reardon, Vasyl Yurchyshyn
arxiv-2111-05812.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Yi Chai, Dale E. Gary, Kevin P. Reardon, Vasyl Yurchyshyn. Waves and oscillations are important solar phenomena, not only because they can propagate and dissipate energy in the chromosphere, but also because they carry information about the structure of the atmosphere in which they propagate. The nature of the three-minute oscillations observed in the umbral region of sunspots is considered to be an effect of propagation of magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) waves upward from below the photosphere.

arxiv-2212-06710.title: TIER: Text-Image Entropy Regularization for Medical CLIP-style models
arxiv-2212-06710.creator: Anil Palepu, Andrew Beam
arxiv-2212-06710.description: Abstract In this paper, we introduce a novel regularization scheme on contrastive language-image pre-trained (CLIP) medical vision models. Our approach is based on the observation that on many medical imaging tasks text tokens should only describe a small number of image regions and, likewise, each image region should correspond to only a few text tokens.

arxiv-2212-11772.title: A Self-Adjusting Fusion Representation Learning Model for Unaligned Text-Audio Sequences
arxiv-2212-11772.creator: Kaicheng Yang, Ruxuan Zhang, Hua Xu, Kai Gao
arxiv-2212-11772.description: Abstract Inter-modal interaction plays an indispensable role in multimodal sentiment analysis. Due to different modalities sequences are usually non-alignment, how to integrate relevant information of each modality to learn fusion representations has been one of the central challenges in multimodal learning.

arxiv-2307-01842.title: Universality in the tripartite information after global quenches: spin flip and semilocal charges
arxiv-2307-01842.creator: Vanja Marić
arxiv-2307-01842.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Vanja Marić. We study stationary states emerging after global quenches in which the time evolution is under local Hamiltonians that possess semilocal conserved operators. In particular, we study a model that is dual to quantum XY chain. We show that a localized perturbation in the initial state can turn an exponential decay of spatial correlations in the stationary state into an algebraic decay.

arxiv-2403-00442.title: Ergodic and non-ergodic properties of disordered SU( 3 3 ) chains
arxiv-2403-00442.creator: Bhupen Dabholkar, Fabien Alet
arxiv-2403-00442.description: Abstract Non-abelian symmetries are thought to be incompatible with many-body localization, but have been argued to produce in certain disordered systems a broad non-ergodic regime distinct from many-body localization. In this context, we present a numerical study of properties of highly-excited eigenstates of disordered chains with SU( 3 3 ) symmetry.

arxiv-2410-02776.title: Bypassing the Popularity Bias: Repurposing Models for Better Long-Tail Recommendation Conference: 7th FAccTRec Workshop on Responsible Recommendation at RecSys 2024; October 14–18, 2024; Bari, Italy CCS: Information systems Recommender systems
arxiv-2410-02776.creator: Václav Blahut, Karel Koupil
arxiv-2410-02776.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Václav Blahut, Karel Koupil. Recommender systems play a crucial role in shaping information we encounter online, whether on social media or when using content platforms, thereby influencing our beliefs, choices, and behaviours. Many recent works address the issue of fairness in recommender systems, typically focusing on topics like ensuring equal access to information and opportunities for all individual users or user groups, promoting diverse content to avoid filter bubbles and echo chambers, enhancing transparency and explainability, and adhering to ethical and sustainable practices.

arxiv-2412-03658.title: Exploring velocity dispersion anisotropy in a dark matter dominated ultra-diffuse galaxy with modified gravity models
arxiv-2412-03658.creator: Esha Bhatia, Sayan Chakrabarti, Sovan Chakraborty
arxiv-2412-03658.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Esha Bhatia, Sayan Chakrabarti, Sovan Chakraborty. The kinematics of the ultra-diffuse galaxy (UDG) NGC1052-DF44 is primarily influenced by the presence of dark matter (DM). In this paper, we conduct a contrasting kinematic study of DF44 within the alternative modified gravity framework.

arxiv-2505-23051.title: Global resistive MHD accretion flows around spinning AGNs: impact of resistivity on MAD state
arxiv-2505-23051.creator: Ramiz Aktar, Kuo-Chuan Pan, Toru Okuda
arxiv-2505-23051.description: Abstract In this study, we investigate the effect of resistivity on the dynamics of global magnetohydrodynamic accretion flows (Res-MHD) around a spinning supermassive black hole. We perform a comparative study of 2D and 3D resistive models around black holes. We examine accretion flow dynamics considering globally uniform resistivity values, ranging from ∼ 0 \sim 0 to 0.1.

arxiv-2510-06867.title: On the emergence of quantum Darwinism and pointer states for non-commuting evolutions
arxiv-2510-06867.creator: Diana A. Chisholm, G. Massimo Palma, Luca Innocenti
arxiv-2510-06867.description: Abstract Quantum systems achieve objectivity by redundantly encoding information about themselves into the surrounding environment, through a mechanism known as quantum Darwinism. When this happens, observes measure the environment and infer the system to be in one of its pointer states.

arxiv-2601-22644.title: Nonlocal Corrections to Scalar Field Effective Action in de Sitter spacetime
arxiv-2601-22644.creator: Will Cerne 1 , Teruaki Suyama 1 1 Department of Physics, Institute of Science Tokyo, 2-12-1 Ookayama, Meguro-ku, Tokyo 152-8551, Japan cerne.w.57e6@m.isct.ac.jp
arxiv-2601-22644.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Will Cerne 1 , Teruaki Suyama 1 1 Department of Physics, Institute of Science Tokyo, 2-12-1 Ookayama, Meguro-ku, Tokyo 152-8551, Japan cerne.w.57e6@m.isct.ac.jp. We investigate the one-loop effective action for a test scalar field in a general Friedmann-Lemaître-Robertson-Walker (FLRW) background, specifically focusing on quantum corrections up to the second order in the interaction strength.

arxiv-2602-00272.creator: ​​Wan Fokkink Department of Computer Science, Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, Georgios Karlos Department of Computer Science, Paderborn University, Andy S. Tatman Bernoulli Institute, University of Groningen

plos-pone-0006641.creator: Julius Halaschek-Wiener, Mahsa Amirabbasi-Beik, Nasim Monfared et al.
plos-pone-0006641.description: PLOS ONE research article. Individuals who live to 85 and beyond without developing major age-related diseases may achieve this, in part, by lacking disease susceptibility factors, or by possessing resistance factors that enhance their ability to avoid disease and prolong lifespan. pmc-10606247.title: Is Marfan Syndrome Associated with Primary Structural Changes in the Left Atrium?
pmc-10606247.creator: Kun Zhang, Lucas Ernst, Isabel Schobert, Karla Philipp, Georg Böning, Frank R Heinzel, Leif-Hendrik Boldt, Petra Gehle, Michel Noutsias
pmc-10606247.description: Marfan syndrome (MFS) is an autosomal-dominant multisystem connective tissue disorder that is based on mutations in the FBN1 gene and variably affects different organs, including the heart. In this study, we investigated cardiac function with a focus on the left atrium (LA) in a relatively large cohort of patients with MFS.

pmc-10735686.title: TO CHOOSE OR NOT TO CHOOSE: CAN AFFECTIVE OR COGNITIVE MECHANISMS EXPLAIN AGE DIFFERENCES IN DECISION AVOIDANCE?
pmc-10735686.creator: Julia Nolte, Corinna Löckenhoff
pmc-10735686.description: Older adults are more likely to avoid decisions, which puts them at risk of experiencing negative consumer or health outcomes. Because the underlying reasons remain unclear, this pre-registered online study assessed the roles of (1) affect (especially regret), (2) subjective difficulty, and (3) cognitive ability in explaining age-related differences in decision avoidance.

pmc-11692764.title: PROGRESSION TO FRAILTY – THE ROLE OF MUSCLE RESILIENCE
pmc-11692764.creator: LaDora Thompson, Lais Perazza
pmc-11692764.description: The impact of a stressful event within the progression to frailty is unknown. In this study we determined the response to an acute stress in Robust, Prefrail, and Frail mice. We hypothesized the Robust mice would show greater resilience compared to Prefrail and Frail mice following a stressful event; whereas the Prefrail mice would show an intermediary resilience status.

pmc-12568936.title: The number of phosphorus loss events will increase with variability and seasonality in far future climate scenarios
pmc-12568936.creator: Golnaz Ezzati, Conor Murphy, Adrian L Collins, Per-Erik Mellander
pmc-12568936.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Climate change is likely to add further pressures to water quality degradation across the globe. The development of robust climate-smart mitigation measures necessitates understanding the impact of extreme hydrological events on catchment hydrology and nutrient losses.

pmc-12653687.title: Multilayered Regulation of Fungal Phosphate Metabolism: From Molecular Mechanisms to Ecological Roles in the Global Phosphorus Cycle
pmc-12653687.creator: Yanan Tan, Yanda Ning, Siyi Wang, Faqin Li, Xuewei Cao, Qin Wang, Ang Ren, Uri Gophna
pmc-12653687.description: Phosphates are essential nutrients for living organisms, and they are involved in various biological processes, including lipid metabolism, energy synthesis, and signal regulation. Recent studies have elucidated the fundamental components and transport proteins of phosphate signaling pathways, thereby providing a more profound understanding of phosphate metabolism in fungi.

pmc-12721223.title: Development of an Evaluation Index System for Health Recommender Systems Based on the Health Technology Assessment Framework: Cross-Sectional Delphi Study
pmc-12721223.creator: Yue Sun, Shijie Hou, Siye Chen, Minmin Leng, Zhiwen Wang
pmc-12721223.description: BackgroundHealth recommender systems (HRSs) are digital platforms designed to deliver personalized health information, resources, and interventions tailored to users’ specific needs. However, existing evaluations of HRSs largely focus on algorithmic performance, with limited scientific evidence supporting user-centered assessment approaches and insufficiently defined evaluation metrics.

pmc-12732973.title: The Template-Jumping Editing Approach in F9-Associated Hemophilia B Gene Therapy
pmc-12732973.creator: Robert Sattarov, Alexey Kuznetsov, Valeriy Klimko, Elena Ignatyeva, Roman Ivanov, Alexander Karabelsky, Anastasia Fizikova
pmc-12732973.description: Hemophilia B is a hereditary bleeding disorder caused by mutations localized throughout the F9 gene. Existing gene therapy products containing AAV vectors have significant limitations. Replacement therapy with coagulation factor FIX infusions is not an optimal way of treatment, as patients still have periodic bleeding and require frequent transfusions.

pmc-13055336.title: Adverse childhood experiences and cognitive outcomes among older adults in low-income and middle-income countries: a systematic review
pmc-13055336.creator: Che Henry Ngwa, Sawsan Abdulrahim, Rim Nehme, Meiya Saad, Mayssan Kabalan, Maria Rita Lteif, Yara Yazbek, Monique Chaaya, Martine Elbejjani
pmc-13055336.description: ObjectivesWhile adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) have been consistently linked to poorer cognitive outcomes in later life, far less is known about ACEs’ contribution to dementia and cognitive ageing risk in low-income and middle-income countries (LMICs), despite their growing and disproportionate share of global Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias (ADRD) burden.

pmc-13343028.title: Incidence and predictors of immediate postoperative haemodynamic instability among adult surgical patients in Ethiopia, 2024: a multicentre prospective observational study
pmc-13343028.creator: Getachew Mekete Deress, Abdurehman Seid Mohammed, Shimelis Seid Tegegne, Habtie Bantider Wubet, Temesgen Birlie Asmare, Kumlachew Geta Belete, Negesse Zurbachew Gobezie, Kaletsidk Dessalegn Mossie, Temesgen Dessie Mengistu, Worknew Ebabu Mengistu, Denberu Eshetie
pmc-13343028.description: AbstractObjectiveThis study aimed to find the incidence and predictors of postoperative haemodynamic instability among adult surgical patients in the postanaesthesia care unit (PACU).Study designA multicentre prospective observational study was conducted from 1 June to 30 September 2024.SettingThe study was conducted at three hospitals in the South Gondar Zone, north-west Ethiopia.

pmc-13557816.title: Hand hygiene adherence and associated factors among nursing staff in long-term care facilities: A cross-sectional study
pmc-13557816.creator: Eunkyo Kim, Eunhee Cho, Gwang Suk Kim, Kyung Hee Lee
pmc-13557816.description: PurposeDespite the critical importance of hand hygiene (HH) in long-term care facilities, research on adherence and its determinants in these settings remains scarce. This study examined HH adherence and its associated factors among nursing staff in long-term care facilities.MethodsThis cross-sectional study surveyed 128 nursing staff members (registered nurses, n=78; nurse assistants, n=50).

pmc-13657372.title: Spatial Choroidal Analysis under Mid-Phase Hyperfluorescent Plaques Demonstrates Unique Signatures in Central Serous Chorioretinopathy: Macula Society International Central Serous Chorioretinopathy Research Network Report Number 20
pmc-13657372.creator: Giulia Gregori, Niroj Kumar Sahoo, Nasiq Hasan, Atharva Ajay Vichare, Shreyaa Rohindra Lall, Sharat Chandra Vupparaboina, Adarsh Gadari, Oscar Matteo Gagliardi, Marco Lupidi, Cesare Mariotti, Stanley Saju, Jessica Cao, Charles C. Wykoff, Kiran Kumar Vupparaboina, Sandeep Chandra Bollepalli, Lihteh W
pmc-13657372.description: PurposeTo evaluate the spatial relationship between mid-phase hyperfluorescent plaques (MPHP) and choroidal vascularity in central serous chorioretinopathy (CSCR) using choroidal vascularity index (CVI) heat maps and enrichment ratio (ER) analysis.DesignRetrospective multicenter study.SubjectsForty eyes from 40 patients with CSCR presenting MPHP on indocyanine green angiography (ICGA) at both baseline and follow-up were included.
